title: Extracts from Adam's Diary, translated from the original ms.

knight_criteria.rationale: The story is a humorous retelling of the Eden myth. Eve's musing about carnivore teeth is folk observation, not a materially represented scientific fact, theory, discovery, or natural/speculative science driving the story.
No device, engineered system, or invention materially affects the setting or outcome. Signs, barrels, and a summer-resort notion are comic contemporary trivialities, not consequential inventions.

The story is set in a mythic biblical past (Eden, Adam and Eve, mastodons, the dodo), which could be read as a remote-past setting, but it is a legendary/theological frame rather than a speculative prehistoric science premise, so materiality is uncertain.

Consequences follow from the Fall premise (death entering the world, having to work, wearing clothes), which resembles extrapolation from a premise, but the premise is theological rather than a scientific/technological/social one, making materiality uncertain.

Adam repeatedly observes, hypothesizes (fish, kangaroo, bear, parrot), attempts experiments and traps, classifies, and revises conclusions about the child. This parodies naturalist classification and systematic inference, but it is deliberately comic and wrong, so its status as genuine scientific method is interpretively uncertain.
The setting is terrestrial (Eden/Niagara region); there are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them.

The Fall introduces death into the world, with all beasts suddenly destroying each other across the plain\u2014a large-scale, causally central calamity repeatedly called a disaster/catastrophe. Whether this mythic-comic event counts as a qualifying catastrophe is interpretively uncertain.
